findings: Diagnostic tool lists/evaluates/clicks/captures/navigates/reloads arbitrary CDP targets; it contains no file-duplicate algorithm or correctness verification.
Target matching accepts prefix in either direction and takes first match without ambiguity check; truncated IDs can select unintended target among matching candidates.

send_command uses a fresh websocket per command, correlates result by message ID and has a response deadline. Initial HTTP target enumeration uses blocking urlopen without explicit timeout inside async function.

Runtime.evaluate exceptionDetails are printed but do not explicitly cause nonzero exit; missing target/element also prints and returns. CLI success code therefore is not proof requested operation succeeded.

Click computes element center without visibility/obscuration/scroll checks. Query selector is JSON-encoded for lookup, but raw selector is also interpolated into a single-quoted error string, so quotes can break that generated expression.
Screenshot writes supplied path and CDP eval can execute arbitrary expressions; those capabilities were not invoked. No browser/user data inspected.
limits: Read-only static review, no imports, websocket/HTTP connections, diagnostic commands or screenshots executed.
67/84 whole files reviewed. No production library change.
